title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 57-63). Grothendieck axiomatizes an 'analysis situs' through a system (𝓕, ≤) of 'figures' satisfying axioms C1-C3. These give a lattice-like structure with an empty figure, finite Sup and a distributivity used on p. 57. On p. 61 he shows that when every figure is finite, such systems are equivalent to triples (M, ≤, R):
- M is the poset of 'strata' (the indecomposable figures).
- R is a reflexive, symmetric relation that is stable under passing to smaller elements.
- Figures are the finite down-closed subsets A ⊂ M with (x, y) ∈ R for all x, y ∈ A.
He then defines connectedness in purely lattice terms. F is connected if F = F' ⊔ F'' (disjoint, i.e. F' ∩ F'' = ∅_𝓕) forces F' = F or F'' = F. F is '0-connexe' if it is connected and nonempty, following his usual SGA convention. A connected component of F is a 0-connected F0 with F = F0 ⊔ G.

This page:
1. Lemma (stated at the foot of p. 61). If F = F' ⊔ F'' and G ⊂ F is a connected subfigure, then G ⊂ F' or G ⊂ F''. Proof: by distributivity (p. 57), G = G' ⊔ G'' with G' = G ∩ F' and G'' = G ∩ F''. Connectedness gives G' = ∅ or G'' = ∅, hence G ⊂ F'' or G ⊂ F'.
2. Corollary 1. Two connected components F0, F1 of F are either equal or disjoint. In the disjoint case F = F0 ⊔ F1 ⊔ H.
3. Corollary 2 (crossed out). A family of pairwise distinct components generates their disjoint sum ⊔F_i ⊂ F, and if the family is finite then F = (⊔F_i) ⊔ H.
4. A crossed-out remark that it is not evident in general that a nonempty figure has a connected component. Some finiteness is needed, and it holds a fortiori for finite figures.
5. Proposition. Let A = F̄ ⊂ M be the set of strata of F, viewed as an ordered set. A subfigure F0 is a connected component of F iff F̄0 is a connected component of A (connectedness of the poset, i.e. of its Alexandrov space / comparability graph). This gives a bijection between components of F and of A.
6. Next page: F is the disjoint sum of its components. The same decomposition is done for M = ⊔ M_i, with 𝓕 embedding into ∏𝓕_i.

Purpose: to set up π0 (the zeroth step of a combinatorial homotopy theory of figures/stratified sets) within this axiomatic 'tame' analysis situs. It is the standard theory of connected components transported to the lattice-of-figures and stratified-poset model.
errors: The lemma at the bottom of p. 61 says 'sous-figure connexe de G'; it must be 'de F'.
In the proof, the dichotomy is written 'G' = ∅ or G'' = G'. This is correct but asymmetric; the intended statement is G' = ∅ or G'' = ∅.
Corollary 1 tacitly uses distributivity again: F1 = F0 ⊔ (F1 ∩ G0) together with connectedness of F1 when F0 ⊂ F1. It is not spelled out, but it is fine.

Existence of connected components for arbitrary (non-finite) figures is acknowledged as non-obvious and left open (crossed-out passage). It is only settled under finiteness, where it reduces to finite posets.

ideas.what: Connectedness and connected components defined lattice-theoretically: no nontrivial complemented splitting F = F' ⊔ F''. Includes the convention '0-connexe' = connected and nonempty.
ideas.modern_name: Connected (indecomposable) elements of a distributive lattice; connected objects in an extensive category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore / lattice theory; the '0-connexe' convention is Grothendieck's (SGA)
ideas.where_published: The n-connected terminology appears in SGA/EGA; this specific lattice version is unsure

ideas.what: A connected subobject of a disjoint sum lies in one summand; distinct components are disjoint; a finite object is the disjoint sum of its components.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary π0 theory in extensive categories / distributive lattices

ideas.what: Components of a figure correspond bijectively to connected components of its poset of strata.
ideas.modern_name: π0 of a finite poset / Alexandrov (finite T0) space; components of a stratified space via its exit-path or stratum poset

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification of connected-component theory inside Grothendieck's axiomatic 'figures' framework. The broader 1986 framework (figures ↔ (M, ≤, R)) may be little known, but nothing on this page goes beyond standard facts about distributive lattices and finite posets.
transcription_corrections: 'Je n'est pas évident' should read 'Il n'est pas évident'.
'l'ensemble des ses obtenues' is likely 'l'ens. de ses strates' (A = F̄ ⊂ M, the set of strata of F).
'l'ens. ouvert A' is more plausibly 'l'ens. ordonné A' (connected component of the ordered set A).
'(qui est l'adhérence par s)' is uncertain; probably a parenthetical about the order induced on A.
In Corollary 1 the formula reads F = F0 ⊔ F1 ⊔ H, with the H scribbled or overwritten rather than cleanly deleted.
The marginal 'c M' next to A = F̄ means A = F̄ ⊂ M.
